title: 2021 Fall AMC 10A Problem 13
statement: Each of \(6\) balls is randomly and independently painted either black or white with equal probability. What is the probability that every ball is different in color from more than half of the other \(5\) balls?

solutions.text:
Note that for this restriction to hold, there must be \(3\) balls of each color.

There are \(2^6 = 64\) ways to color the balls and \(\binom{6}{3} = 20\) to choose which balls are white.

The desired probability is therefore \(\dfrac{20}{64} = \dfrac{5}{16}.\)

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Each ball must see at least \(3\) balls of the other color
That forces exactly \(3\) balls of each color
